issues: The final paragraph implies the Monte Carlo cross-check sets the Hull-White function apart, but the Vasicek record also simulates the short rate.

vasicek_interest_rate_model.text:
`hull_white_short_rate_model` and `vasicek_interest_rate_model` use the same dynamics and the same closed-form zero-coupon bond price. With a constant mean-reversion level, `hull_white_short_rate_model` literally delegates to the Vasicek function, so the two give the same model. It is not a genuine time-dependent Hull-White fit to an observed market forward curve.

The differences are mostly in the interface. In `hull_white_short_rate_model` the mean-reversion level is called `theta_const` and has a default of 0.03, while `vasicek_interest_rate_model` takes `theta` as a required long-run mean. The default seeds also differ: 103 for the Hull-White function and 101 for Vasicek.

Use `vasicek_interest_rate_model` to ask what a bond is worth, and how the short rate might evolve, under a plain mean-reverting Gaussian rate. Use `hull_white_short_rate_model` for the same question when you want it framed as the extended-Vasicek form with a constant level, with a Monte Carlo cross-check beside the analytic price.

explain.text: `hull_white_short_rate_model` prices a zero-coupon bond under a one-factor short-rate model where the rate follows `dr = κ(θ−r)dt + σ dW`. You give it the starting rate `r0`, the mean-reversion speed `kappa`, the volatility `sigma` and the bond `maturity`. It returns an analytic bond price and a Monte Carlo cross-check, which you can tune with `n_steps`, `n_simulations` and `seed`. With the constant level `theta_const`, it simply calls `vasicek_interest_rate_model`, so it is not a time-dependent Hull-White fit to a market forward curve.

when.text:
`hull_white_short_rate_model` fits when you want a simple mean-reverting short-rate model with a constant long-run level.

- You want a closed-form zero-coupon bond price from `r0`, `kappa`, `sigma`, `maturity` and `theta_const`, plus a Monte Carlo cross-check of it.
- You want to see how mean-reversion speed and volatility shape a bond price under `dr = κ(θ−r)dt + σ dW`.
- You are fine with a constant `theta_const`. In that case it gives the same result as the Vasicek model, so it is not a time-dependent Hull-White fit to an observed market forward curve.
- You want to compare the simulation with the analytic price by adjusting `n_steps`, `n_simulations` and `seed`.

If you need a short rate that stays non-negative, `cox_ingersoll_ross_model` is listed as giving a closed-form ZCB price and a simulated non-negative short rate.
